items.prompt:
A reversible reaction can
A) go forward and backward
B) go only forward
C) go only backward
D) never happen

Chemical equilibrium is when the forward and backward reactions happen at
A) the same rate
B) no rate
C) opposite times
D) random speeds

steps: Equilibrium is equal forward and backward rates.

items.prompt:
At equilibrium, the amounts of reactants and products
A) stay steady
B) always rise
C) always fall
D) disappear

Adding more reactant shifts the balance toward more
A) products
B) reactants
C) nothing
D) gas only

steps: Extra reactant drives the forward reaction.

items.prompt:
Removing product as it forms shifts the balance toward more
A) products
B) reactants
C) heat
D) nothing

steps: Removing product drives the forward reaction.

items.prompt:
At equilibrium, reactions are
A) still happening at equal rates
B) completely stopped
C) only going forward
D) only going backward
items.answer: A) still happening at equal rates

steps: Both reactions continue at equal rates.

items.prompt:
Amounts stay steady at equilibrium because
A) products form as fast as they turn back, since the rates are equal
B) all reactions stop
C) only one direction occurs
D) matter is destroyed
items.answer: A) products form as fast as they turn back, since the rates are equal

items.prompt:
To make more product from a reversible reaction, a chemist could
A) add more reactant or remove product
B) remove all reactant
C) stop the reaction
D) add product
items.answer: A) add more reactant or remove product
